title: Sebastian's Cotton Club audition; refusing Lionel Hampton as drummer
summary: Frank Sebastian liked the band but wanted Lionel Hampton as drummer; Barefield refused, kept Lee Young, and got the job anyway, staying seven or eight months.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Where were you playing with this band?
We was playing at San Bernadino.
What kind of a place was it?

It was just a ballroom. So we come back and I go out and see Frank Sebastian to make an audition for the Cotton Club. So we went out and made an audition and he liked the band. So he told me, he said, 'I like the band. I'd like to bring your -- Lionel had his band in there already. But he said, 'I'd like to bring your band in but I want you to use Lionel on drums.' And I wouldn't take it. I told him, well, I have a drummer, I have a fellow who's been playing with me ever since we got together, Lee Young was my drummer. And I said, if you ever feel like you could use the band like it is, I'll consider it.'
So two weeks later he called me and we went out

there to work. And we stayed out there about four or five -- seven or eight months at Sebastian's Cotton Club. Then when we left the Cotton Club they brought two bands in there, Les Hite and Jimmy Dorsey. And they put a two-band policy.

But then I played up and down the coast there with my band for a while. And finally work wasn't -- there wasn't enough work. I couldn't get no bookings to come back East. I wanted to come back East. So Ethel Waters came out and took Don Byas and Tyree Glenn and she had the band --
